name: Kodjoviakope and Nyekonakpoe
tagline: The embassy quarter by the Ghana border
description: The western neighbourhoods running down to the Ghanaian frontier, holding the embassies, the international schools, the better hotels and much of the expatriate housing. Streets are wider and quieter here, and the beach road runs along the southern edge.
bestFor: Anyone wanting security, reliable services and the border close
pros: Best housing and infrastructure in the city
Walking distance to the Ghana border crossing
cons: Quiet to the point of dull
A car or taxi is needed for the centre

name: The Administrative Quarter
tagline: The centre, the Grand Marche and the ministries
description: The core of the city between Boulevard du 13 Janvier and the sea, with the Grand Marche, the Independence Monument, the banks and the government buildings. It is dense, busy and where the commercial life of Togo actually happens.
bestFor: Short stays and anyone needing banks or ministries
pros: Grand Marche and the central commerce
cons: Real theft risk around the market
Avoided by most people after dark

name: Tokoin
tagline: The hill district with the university and the hospital
description: The elevated residential area north of the centre, holding the University of Lome, the main teaching hospital and a large spread of ordinary housing. It is where much of the city's professional population lives and it is noticeably cooler than the coast.
bestFor: Longer stays at local prices with services nearby
pros: Local rents rather than expatriate ones
cons: Traffic on the routes into the centre

name: Be
tagline: The traditional quarter and the fetish market
description: The old Ewe quarter east of the centre, dense and entirely local, holding the sacred forest, the Be lagoon and, at its edge, the Akodessewa fetish market that is the largest of its kind anywhere. It is the most culturally intense part of Lome.
bestFor: Anyone here to understand the city rather than be comfortable in it
pros: Cheapest food and rents in the city
cons: Dense, hot and hard to navigate
Drainage and waste problems in the rains

name: Baguida and Avepozo
tagline: The beach strip east of the city
description: The coastal road east towards Benin, where the beach hotels, weekend resorts and a run of restaurants sit facing the Gulf of Guinea. It is quieter and greener than the city, about twenty minutes from the centre, and the beaches here are the usable ones.
bestFor: Anyone wanting the beach and space away from the centre
pros: The best beaches within reach of Lome
Quieter and greener than the city
cons: Swimming is dangerous on much of this coast
